# Brian Merchant

I’m a writer, reporter and author based in Los Angeles. I write the newsletter [BLOOD IN THE MACHINE.](https://www.bloodinthemachine.com/) I’m also a reporter in residence at the AI Now Institute. My work has appeared in the New York Times, WIRED, Harper’s, the Guardian, and beyond. Previously, I was the technology columnist at [the _Los Angeles Times_](https://www.latimes.com/people/brian-merchant) and the senior editor at Motherboard (RIP). I’m the author of [The One Device: the Secret History of the iPhone](https://www.littlebrown.com/titles/brian-merchant/the-one-device/9780316546119/) (2017, Little, Brown) and [Blood in the Machine: the Origins of the Rebellion against Big Tech](https://www.hachettebookgroup.com/titles/brian-merchant/blood-in-the-machine/9780316487740/) (2023, Little, Brown), and a founder of VICE’s speculative fiction outlet [Terraform](https://www.vice.com/en/topic/terraform) . We published a best-of anthology, _[Terraform: Watch/Worlds/Burn](https://us.macmillan.com/books/9780374602666/terraform) ,_ with MCD Books, in 2022.

My email is **briancmerchant at gmail dot com** , my Twitter is [here](https://twitter.com/bcmerchant) , and my speaker’s bureau, BrightSight, can be [contacted here](https://www.brightsightspeakers.com/speakers-a-z/brian-merchant) .

_Image via [the New Yorker](https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2023/10/30/revenge-of-the-luddites) ._

Welcome to my expanded biographical blogroll. So, I’m a technology journalist who frequently writes about automation, labor, and how tech impacts the environment, among other things. I’ve also covered the climate crisis, biodiversity loss, and clean energy. I’m the author of a bestselling book about the iPhone, [_the One Device._](https://www.amazon.com/One-Device-Secret-History-iPhone/dp/031654616X) I’m currently at work on a second book, about the first rebellion against automation—the deeply misunderstood Luddite uprisings of the early 1800s—and what might cause the next one.

ludddd

For those interested in a longer-winded and necessarily self-laudatory detailing of my work, here is some more about me:

The _One Device_ was shortlisted for [some nice awards](https://ig.ft.com/sites/business-book-award/books/2017/shortlist/the-one-device-by-brian-merchant/) , and was recently [optioned for a limited series](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/iphone-history-one-device-optioned-tv-by-echo-lake-1135647) . It has been translated into a dozen languages.

My recent feature [“Click Here to Kill,”](https://harpers.org/archive/2020/01/click-here-to-kill-dark-web-hitman/) was the cover story for the January 2020 issue of _Harper’s Magazine._ In 2019, I ran a project called [Automaton](https://gizmodo.com/tag/automaton) at Gizmodo, in which I investigated and opined about automation, AI, and the future of work.

My writing has appeared in _The New York Times, Harper’s Magazine,_ _Wired, the Atlantic, the LA Times, the_ _Guardian_ , _Slate_ , _VICE Magazine_ , _the Verge, Gizmodo,_ _the Outline,_ _Fast Company_ , _Fortune_ , _Paste_ _,_ and elsewhere. For years, I was a writer and editor at Motherboard, VICE’s science and technology outlet, where I founded Terraform, its online fiction site. I still run [Terraform,](https://motherboard.vice.com/en_us/topic/terraform) which publishes a piece of speculative fiction each week—for info on what I’m looking for and [how to submit stories, go here](https://motherboard.vice.com/en_us/article/kbzxpa/how-to-submit-stories-to-terraform) . I’ve produced some short documentaries, too—my feature on Soylent was included on the late and great David Carr’s [final syllabus.](https://medium.com/press-play/press-play-4b26bed77b7d)

I’ve also published a work or two of short fiction, including [The Convoy](https://motherboard.vice.com/en_us/article/bjqxxm/the-convoy) , which was picked up by [Boing Boing](https://boingboing.net/2019/01/24/i-can-tell-by-the-voxels.html) (where Cory Doctorow called it “skillful” and “eerily plausible”), Digg (which called it “today’s best short story”), and the front page of Vice.com. **Brian Merchant** is an American technology journalist and author. His work often focuses on social and environmental issues relating to technology and tech companies. [[ 1 ]]() His writing has appeared in publications including _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ , [_Wired_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wired_\(magazine\) "Wired (magazine)") , [_Slate_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate_\(magazine\) "Slate (magazine)") , _[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")_ , and _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ . [[ 1 ]]() He was the technology columnist at the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ in from 2023 to early 2024. He has written two books, _The One Device: the Secret History of the iPhone_ (2017) and _Blood in the Machine: the Origins of the Rebellion against Big Tech_ (2023).

He currently works full time reporting for his [Substack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substack "Substack") newsletter, _Blood in the Machine_ , where he reports on how big tech and developments in generative AI affect workers and consumers. [[ 2 ]](:2-2)

## Biography

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brian_Merchant&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography") ]

Merchant is from Sacramento, California. He is a graduate of [UC Santa Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Santa_Barbara "UC Santa Barbara") . [[ 1 ]]()

While at [Vice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_\(magazine\) "Vice (magazine)") , he co-founded Terraform, a speculative fiction section of [Motherboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motherboard_magazine "Motherboard magazine") . [[ 1 ]]() [[ 3 ]]()

In January 2023, he became the technology columnist at the _Los Angeles Times_ . [[ 1 ]]() In January 2024, Merchant was laid off in a wave of layoffs exceeding 20% of newsroom staff at the _Los Angeles Times_ . [[ 4 ]]()

In February 2025, Merchant began working full time reporting for his Substack newsletter _Blood in the Machine_ . [[ 2 ]](:2-2)

Brian Merchant is a writer, tech journalist, and the author of a bestselling book about the iPhone, The One Device. His most recent book is Blood in the Machine: The Origins of the Rebellion Against Big Tech (2023). He has been the Los Angeles Times ' tech columnist, an editor at Motherboard, VICE’s science and technology publication, and the founder of Terraform, its online fiction site. He founded Automaton, a project that examined the human impact of AI and automation, for Gizmodo. Exclusively represented by BrightSight Speakers, he currently serves as Journalist in Residence, AI Now Institute. Brian is also the co-editor of a print anthology of Terraform stories, called Terraform: Watch/Worlds/Burn (2022). His work has appeared in the New York Times, Harper's, Wired, the Atlantic, the Guardian, Slate, the Washington Post, Fast Company, Fortune, and beyond. He lives in Los Angeles.

How AI will transform the way we work

Lessons from the Industrial Revolution, the Luddites — on through today.

AI is fast on the rise as the revolutionary new tech of the day. But technology and automation have been disrupting and reorganizing the way humans work for over two hundred years.
